Recent research separates plausible explanations from faithful evidence. “Walk the Talk?” (2025) evaluates whether concepts cited in explanations actually affect model outputs through counterfactual input changes; useful for checking whether cited historical items influence a GRU4Rec recommendation. This measures model dependence, not the user’s actual rejection reason. A 2025 movie study found positive explanations preferred by 129 participants, illustrating that perceived explanation quality alone does not establish diagnostic validity. [Faithfulness study](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/walk-the-talk-measuring-the-faithfulness-of-large-language-model-explanations/), [movie explanation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03376).

Practical synthesis for the restricted data: fit TF–IDF, optionally reduced with locally fitted SVD, on permitted titles/descriptions. Measure recent-history similarity with timestamp decay as “recent-intent support”; measure strongest historical and within-list textual overlap as “possible redundancy.” Attach supporting item IDs, dates, and matching text to each annotation. These are proposed proxies, not established measurements of intent or functional equivalence. Similar descriptions cannot establish ownership, compatibility, unmet needs, mood, or diversity/conformity traits. Missing descriptions, ambiguous matches, or contradictory evidence should yield “insufficient information.”

Abstention research (2024) shows uncertainty-based withholding can improve reliability in question answering; transfer to recommendation annotations requires validation. MetaFaith (2025) likewise finds verbal confidence often misaligned with uncertainty. Where explicit feedback exists, evaluate each proxy against the corresponding stated reason using held-out users, precision/recall, calibration, uncertainty intervals, and coverage versus error as abstention thresholds vary. Keep simulator feedback distinct from real-user feedback. Without explicit reason labels, report proxy distributions and evidence coverage; rejection-reason accuracy remains unmeasured. [Abstention study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.10960), [MetaFaith](https://research.google/pubs/metafaith-faithful-natural-language-uncertainty-expression-in-llms/).
